shoal_e23_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_entry.text: On Day Four Hundred Fifteen, Yue attended the first of the chosen road's two accepted one-hour preparation visits. Her port employment and powered reassessment were complete. This was the finite unpaid preparation she had agreed before the two paid mine receiving days. The current role determined which property, people, and permissions she would actually receive. Her own pack remained separate, with no unchosen kit or cargo hidden inside it.

shoal_e23_convoy_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_01.text: The gallery keeper opened the permitted outside inventory of six numbered signal-plate crates. Lin checked each visible number against the current owner list with the keeper present. A mark on the third crate looked like an eight until viewed in better ordinary light. They corrected the transport copy's reading without altering the physical owner's mark. It was a receiving correction, not permission to open every crate and inspect private plate geometry.

shoal_e23_convoy_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_02.text: The keeper had retained custody through the preliminary visit. Today's one-hour work confirmed what the ordinary packer and carrier would later receive. Lin would become the named escort when the carrier took its actual transport scope, while the crates remained port property. The current handover did not make her a plate owner or give the supplier bench authority over her private bodily notes. Both source and person had their own limits.

shoal_e23_convoy_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_03.text: The ordinary packer examined the six crates under the accepted four-copper packing scope. Two covers needed suitable new wrapping before the road, while the underlying cases remained serviceable under the current ordinary check. He performed the accepted wrapping and outside labels on Day Four Hundred Seventeen, receiving four after that actual work. His current gallery job paid its own other hours. The small convoy line was no unpaid demand that he pack forever.

shoal_e23_convoy_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_04.text: Lin inspected the performed outside result during her second offered visit, not by reaching overhead or testing strength against a full crate. The keeper and packer showed the actual condition at their ordinary suitable working height. One tie needed reseating before the carrier copy was final. The packer corrected it within the accepted scope. The current record retained the observed correction rather than presenting packing as something that had never needed adjustment.

shoal_e23_convoy_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_05.text: At the gallery's far wall, she saw the empty ordinary bay reserved for a different future project. Nobody claimed it held another duplicate set of plates. The six current crates were real property in this particular inventory. Other freight questions could remain unfunded. Lin had chosen access to one technical source, which was enough of a change in her next town without making the port a warehouse of every convenient device.

shoal_e23_convoy_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_06.text: The licensed shared carrier arrived for its actual receiving on Day Four Hundred Twenty. Its ordinary workers checked the outside condition, dimensions, permitted load, and selected road scope before accepting the cargo booking. Lin's shoulder restriction remained visible in her personal application. The carrier had appropriate handlers; it would not use her body to replace one because a cultivation stage looked useful on a passenger list.

shoal_e23_convoy_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_07.text: Twenty-four copper prepaid the accepted carrier fare and booked carriage from the convoy source. The present receipt established the reserved transport and actual custody arrangement, not a claim that the road had already been traveled. Physical departure remained on Four Hundred Twenty-Five and arrival planned for Four Hundred Forty. If actual conditions changed, the carrier would use its proper notification process rather than have Lin backdate the movement to protect the timetable.

shoal_e23_convoy_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_08.text: The keeper transferred the six current outside custody records to the named carrier receiving, with Lin identified as the ordinary escort contact under its accepted terms. The crates remained in the gallery's secure holding until actual loading under that arrangement. Lin could report a discrepancy, stop an unsuitable transfer, or ask the proper owner for a decision. She could not secretly repair a plate or sell one to pay a personal supper bill.

shoal_e23_convoy_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_09.text: Rong brought the mine's defined supplier-bench invitation in its offered current form. It named the freight comparison and receiving dates, with qualified supervision and no general entry into every laboratory. Lin read the actual scope and signed only the receiving of the invitation. Accepting a future comparison was not proof the bench would produce a result she liked. Its owners could question her report, and she could retain uncertainty where the observations required it.

shoal_e23_convoy_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_10.text: The current convoy source's four-copper message line paid its actual permitted notices and receiving copies for owner, carrier, and intended mine contact. Those messages identified six port-owned crates. They did not include a private family letter the gallery keeper might separately send. Lin checked the relevant copies within her offered preparation hour and handed them back. The finite paperwork gave other people a real way to know what would reach them.

shoal_e23_convoy_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_11.text: The keeper asked whether she expected to remain at the mine after the two paid days. Lin said she had accepted no later role. He liked that she did not treat his shipment as a ladder into every job there. He had also hoped a familiar escort might help his future customers. She could consider a new offered scope later, but the current source would end on its accepted work and property receiving.

shoal_e23_convoy_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_12.text: At the door, an ordinary worker asked her to remember his complaint about a signal no one had heard in the rain. He offered a current account under a narrow permitted receiving, which did not fit the private technical appendix. Lin directed it to the proper current source process instead of hiding it in the plate case. A cargo escort could care about worker experience without possessing a household-interview post she had not selected.

shoal_e23_convoy_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_13.text: She felt the cost of that refusal. The worker had chosen to ask her because she was leaving toward a technical source, and the current role gave her no accepted way to carry his private account. He could use the public process He Ming was helping develop. Lin told him where its actual ordinary hours were posted and made no promise the supplier would answer sooner because her name accompanied the crates.

shoal_e23_convoy_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_14.text: The carrier workers tested the planned ordinary loading route with their actual equipment before departure day. One cart would turn better from the gallery's wider entrance. The keeper allowed that route and moved an empty rack under his authority. Lin observed from a safe public position and recorded the relevant current receiving. No plate had to be lifted by qi to make the convoy dramatic. Suitable ordinary preparation did the present work.

shoal_e23_convoy_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_15.text: Rong asked whether she would favor the plate owner's claims if the mine's own technician disagreed. Lin said her role required actual receiving and offered findings, not loyalty to a desired conclusion. He accepted the answer because a comparison worth funding could disappoint him. He still hoped it would not. Their agreement preserved that ordinary tension rather than converting a cargo contract into a promise that both would enjoy every result.

shoal_e23_convoy_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_16.text: The other two road arrangements remained outside Lin's property record. The pilots' kit did not enter the carrier case, and the five workers held no interview appointment through her escort. She could greet them in the port as ordinary people if they wished. The next mine would receive her with a sharper supplier source and fewer offered household connections. Her decision now had a physical shape in six numbered crates and a current invitation.

shoal_e23_convoy_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_17.text: Before the second hour ended, she checked the six-number list again with the carrier receiver. Their outside inventory matched. The receiver kept the signed custody copy and Lin received the actual escort extract. She did not take the gallery key. The keeper retained it for his own employer's ongoing work. Finishing her offered preparation left the actual owner able to close the gallery after she walked out.

shoal_e23_convoy_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_18.text: Lin returned to her room with no crate balanced against her shoulder. Her personal pack held the accepted extract and current role copy. The shared carrier would handle the actual load on departure day under its own staffed scope. She reserved her own thirty for meals and shared overnight stays across the road, leaving those costs separate from the cargo owner's booked fare and four funded arrival days.

shoal_e23_convoy_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_19.text: At supper she told He Ming the preparation had finished within its two offered hours. He asked whether the supplier invitation pleased her. She said it did, and that she would miss hearing more travelers' own accounts on the road. He nodded without treating the preference as a betrayal. The port had helped them learn that a finite choice could be useful and incomplete. She would carry that incompleteness beside the crate list.

shoal_e23_convoy_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_convoy_20.text: On Day Four Hundred Twenty-One, the keeper sent the actual final outside inventory acknowledgment. Six crates remained under their chosen transport arrangement, ready for properly staffed loading on the named departure day. Lin's preparation was complete; the mine's paid receiving still future. The convoy source had paid packing four, carrier booking twenty-four, and messages four. Eighteen remained for arrival board eight and her two actual receiving days ten.

shoal_e23_refuge_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_01.text: Bai Fen arrived at the first preparation table carrying a small tile sample she owned. She wanted it in her personal bag, not received as association property. The carrier would examine the ordinary bag under its passenger terms. Lin could see why she kept a sample: a possible employer might understand her skill better from a current object than a vague promise. No mine employer had yet asked to buy it or offered her work.

shoal_e23_refuge_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_02.text: Yan He brought a basket with a lid he had made. He wanted to hear whether its ordinary size fit the actual passenger allowance before loading it with the examples he planned to show. The receiving clerk checked the accepted dimensions. It fit, while another larger basket would not fit the same scope. Yan chose the smaller one and left the other in a separately accepted personal custody, with no association right to sell it.

shoal_e23_refuge_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_03.text: Pei Lu had packed two kitchen tools suited to her own ordinary trade. One was too heavy for the modest bag she wanted to carry. She decided to leave it with a consenting colleague under actual personal terms. Lin did not offer to lift it with qi through fifteen days of travel. Pei wanted an ordinary workable load and knew a town could have tools without her carrying an entire kitchen to it.

shoal_e23_refuge_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_04.text: Xu Zhen reviewed the actual carrier handling arrangement against his preexisting shoulder restrictions. He had a small personal bag and would use the carrier's appropriate ordinary loading rather than test himself publicly. Lin's current body record had its own waist-only limit. Neither restriction healed the other's body. They could agree on suitable handling and keep their own clinical guidance without turning the preparation into a contest over who was less injured.

shoal_e23_refuge_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_05.text: Jin Shu brought a plain wool sample and declined to describe her private family in the group receiving. The clerk required an offered travel contact, not a household narrative. She supplied a permitted receiving address and kept personal letters with her own bag. Lin recorded the narrow current answer and asked no broader question. An optional statement at the mine would remain optional even if someone there thought private detail made a more compelling account.

shoal_e23_refuge_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_06.text: The first offered hour confirmed passenger names, current ordinary bag plans, and accepted contacts. It did not receive all five adults' life histories or hire them for a mine task. He Ming had his own office work afterward and closed the table at its advertised time. Lin's preparation role ended for that day too. The travelers left to complete their actual current livelihoods and personal arrangements before departure.

shoal_e23_refuge_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_07.text: Over the following days, Bai finished an accepted small tile repair under her current client's terms and received its ordinary payment after the client checked it. The road provision she had already reserved remained separate. She kept the sample but left the client's repaired surface where it belonged. Going to another town did not give her permission to abandon current work or remove a finished object merely because it displayed her skill.

shoal_e23_refuge_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_08.text: Yan ended a paid basket order at its actual agreed handover. The buyer objected to a color he had approved earlier. Yan showed the current agreed sample and offered a separately priced change if wanted. The buyer accepted the original work and paid its due price. The disagreement did not require Lin to adjudicate it. Yan arrived at the second preparation with his old job finished and his own current money still his.

shoal_e23_refuge_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_09.text: Pei completed the final kitchen shifts she had accepted before the road. Her employer would arrange later staffing rather than assume she remained available after departure. She disliked leaving a younger colleague with difficult early hours and would not promise to work from another town. They exchanged ordinary contact addresses under their own consent. Lin heard the story only because Pei chose to tell it while waiting at the booking desk.

shoal_e23_refuge_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_10.text: Xu returned a timber tool he had borrowed from his current employer, with an actual condition receiving before the job's ending. His own sample and personal bag remained separate. The employer did not charge him for marks documented before his use. He carried the received ending copy because he had learned that a clean goodbye could still need a clear record. His next lighter-work hope remained a hope, not an employer already named in the mine.

shoal_e23_refuge_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_11.text: Jin settled her current ordinary wool work and received its actual due payment before closing that term. She told the group only that her work was finished. They did not demand private numbers as proof she deserved the road. Appropriate booking had already established her thirty-copper personal provision after current port costs. The current statement source bought no right to inspect every later purchase or correspondence merely because she had accepted a ticket.

shoal_e23_refuge_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_12.text: On Day Four Hundred Twenty, the licensed carrier issued six actual booked road tickets at four copper each, twenty-four paid from the selected source. One belonged to Lin and five to the consenting adults. The receipt reserved the named ordinary road; it did not claim departure or arrival already performed. Their own meals and shared overnight stays across fifteen days remained thirty personal copper each under the accepted living arrangements.

shoal_e23_refuge_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_13.text: The carrier's clerk read the actual start and destination aloud. Yan asked about a later branch road to a different market, which was outside this booked scope. He could arrange it separately if he chose and could afford it. He would not be trapped at the mine because an arrival source wanted his statement. The clerk explained the current transfer process, and Yan kept the mine ticket he had actually accepted for now.

shoal_e23_refuge_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_14.text: Bai asked whether she could refuse an optional statement after using the funded room. Yes. Pei asked whether she could offer a current kitchen-work question instead of a public story about loss. The mine receiver would examine its actual scope with her. Xu said he did not want to provide a statement. Jin said she would decide after hearing the current question. Lin recorded no future statement as completed or paid in advance.

shoal_e23_refuge_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_15.text: The forty-copper arrival line would fund the five adults' four ordinary days of room and meals, separate from Lin's eight-copper four-day board. These were actual future receiving dates, Four Hundred Forty through Forty-Three. No later room had been promised. The travelers had their own plans and margins after the road. Lin could help them identify the proper current office and still leave each person free to refuse an unsuitable offer there.

shoal_e23_refuge_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_16.text: The second offered hour ended with their current tickets and consented contacts checked. He Ming kept the proper source copy and Lin received only the helper extract she needed. She did not acquire control of five bags or a mandate to speak for absent port households. The travelers left the table together and immediately disagreed over where to buy bread. Their small argument was a good reminder that shared travel did not merge six people into one answer.

shoal_e23_refuge_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_17.text: Lin joined them for the walk only because all agreed they wanted company. She bought her own ordinary portion within the already bounded personal extras. Xu found a seat suited to his shoulder, and Yan complained that the bread was too soft. Pei said he could buy a stone if hardness was his first requirement. Jin laughed once and then asked the seller the actual flour price. The road would contain such ordinary conversations too.

shoal_e23_refuge_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_18.text: An interested worker who had stayed in the port greeted them and asked whether there might be another trip later. He Ming could receive a current proposal and would promise no new source before approval. Her actual decision to remain still respected her household's needs. The five did not boast that they were braver for leaving. Different bodies, purses, and obligations made different roads possible at different times.

shoal_e23_refuge_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_19.text: On Day Four Hundred Twenty-One, the clerk confirmed six booked tickets and the proper future arrival scope. Twenty-four of ninety-two had actually paid ticket booking. Sixty-eight remained for ten Lin receiving wage, eight Lin arrival board, forty adults' arrival board, and up to ten optional performed statements. No packing or survey-copy charge appeared in this source. Its accounts matched people and permissions rather than borrowing a neighboring cargo budget.

shoal_e23_refuge_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_refuge_20.text: Lin returned to her room with the helper extract and her own current pack. She would travel without supplier crates, bench access, or the pilots' kit. Instead she had five actual consenting companions with different work, bodies, and answers. The road's first duty would be to meet the carrier at its real departure hour. After that, ordinary days would need ordinary food, rest, receiving, and the patience to let adults choose for themselves.

shoal_e23_survey_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_01.text: The pilots' receiver placed the actual unpowered loan case on a low ordinary table. Lin read its offered inventory while the receiver opened each compartment within the agreed current scope. A plumb, level, and external comparison kit belonged to the association. Their straps and case belonged there too. The list contained no fuel, spirit stones, private supplier appendix, or device meant to qualify a task inside Lin's body.

shoal_e23_survey_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_02.text: The current level's outside scratch matched the preliminary condition note. Its functional check belonged to a qualified ordinary instrument hand, who compared it against the actual reference under the owner's existing maintenance scope. Lin watched from the offered position and received the present report rather than announcing calibration from the appearance of a straight casing. The association wanted a useful borrower who knew when to defer to a different craft.

shoal_e23_survey_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_03.text: One case strap had become looser since its last ordinary use. The owner commissioned the suitable small repair under its own maintenance terms before loan receiving. It did not take the cost from Lin's fifty-copper travel source or ask her to correct it with qi. The current craftsperson completed the repair and the receiver checked the performed work. A tool owner could retain responsibility for present condition before transferring a loan.

shoal_e23_survey_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_04.text: The plumb's line had a knot in the offered length. The instrument hand showed which current use permitted it and where a different hanging arrangement would make it unsuitable. The loan report retained the actual line conditions. Lin could not solve every later mine question by hanging the same tool anywhere and calling its answer independent. A limited instrument could be valuable precisely because its method and limits stayed visible.

shoal_e23_survey_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_05.text: The comparison kit's current reference strip received its own ordinary condition check. It measured a defined external relationship within the accepted scope, not source input, a mineral's hidden intent, or bodily compatibility. Lin asked what a doubtful result should look like in the permitted report. The receiver showed an actual example with its missing conditions plainly named. A report could be usable while conclude that a present comparison remained incomplete.

shoal_e23_survey_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_06.text: During the first offered hour, she received the current condition report and proposed custody terms without taking the case away before final acceptance. The pilots retained it in their own cupboard while repair and booking finished. Lin held only the preliminary extract. The source had licensed a later loan, not a right to rummage through the owner's storage or copy old charts unrelated to her current task.

shoal_e23_survey_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_07.text: The pilots' receiver described a past survey in which a careful figure had been repeated after its condition changed. The number itself had not lied. The later user had treated it as if its original measured place and date did not matter. Lin wrote the current method questions beside the proposed public extract. She wanted the next reader to know which ordinary observation a figure came from before trusting it in a different place.

shoal_e23_survey_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_08.text: A young pilot wanted to add a spare object to the case just in case. It belonged to a separate owner and was outside the inventory. The receiver refused until an actual new permission and suitable scope existed. No one had time to complete that proposal before this loan's preparation ended. The object stayed in the cupboard. Lin's case would contain fewer possibilities and a property history its owners could actually defend.

shoal_e23_survey_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_09.text: On Day Four Hundred Twenty, the repaired and checked case received its final ordinary loan acceptance. Lin compared current items with the offered list beside the receiver. Both copies named the actual condition and handling method. The current property could now enter its selected carrier arrangement under the pilots' ownership. Her acceptance made her responsible for its defined custody and return, not free to sell it, modify it, or keep it as personal equipment.

shoal_e23_survey_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_10.text: The licensed shared carrier accepted the case's ordinary load and booked road scope under its appropriate current handling terms. Twenty-four copper prepaid the accepted fare from the survey source, reserving departure on Four Hundred Twenty-Five. Physical travel remained future. Lin's own thirty would pay personal living for fifteen road days. The tool owner had not promised to feed her indefinitely because its instruments now traveled beside her bag.

shoal_e23_survey_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_11.text: Four copper funded the actual permitted copying performed for current external comparison extracts and owner-approved method notes. Private charts stayed with the pilots. A requested extra sheet exceeded the offered copying scope and was left for a later separate proposal. Lin received the actual useful copies rather than pretending a source with four copper could reproduce the entire chart room. Her next work would begin from a limited honest packet.

shoal_e23_survey_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_12.text: The source's four return-dispatch copper would remain for its actual later return service, not be spent now on unrelated messages. The deadline was Five Hundred, met through the authorized licensed carrier's condition and custody receiving at the mine. Onward physical arrival at the harbor would occur after the actual voyage. The receiver showed the agreed named authority line so an unfamiliar mine clerk could distinguish the proper receiver from anyone merely offering a convenient road.

shoal_e23_survey_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_13.text: Lin read the planned authorized custody date, Four Hundred Ninety-Six, and asked what would happen if present observations required an earlier return. She could arrange the proper service within its terms and notify the owner, rather than keep the tools for their last permitted day because a calendar invited it. If conditions prevented the agreed return, actual notice and a responsible plan were required. Silence would not transform a dated loan into a permanent gift.

shoal_e23_survey_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_14.text: The instrument hand checked the ordinary carrying method against Lin's shoulder limits. The case would travel in the carrier's accepted storage, handled by its suitable workers. Lin could manage the defined light personal inspection at a suitable height without overhead catching. The application record remained part of her own suitability, not a rule forcing another passenger with a different body to copy her method. The current holder needed actual workable terms.

shoal_e23_survey_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_15.text: At the second hour's end, she had the lender's accepted loan extract and condition record. The case remained under the carrier's proper secure holding until departure loading. The pilots kept their original source and cupboard key. Lin had gained instruments and permitted public questions, while the supplier-bench invitation and worker-group interview role remained unavailable. The difference now had physical weight and a real return date.

shoal_e23_survey_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_16.text: The receiver asked whether she wanted to publish her own route practice beside the survey's external findings. She declined. Those private notes served a different body and source. Public ordinary comparisons could be offered within their accepted scope without exposing her internal practice or implying that a survey instrument measured it. The receiver accepted the answer and removed a tentative personal-qualification attachment from the public extract list.

shoal_e23_survey_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_17.text: Lin walked outside with the young pilot after the current work ended. He wanted to know whether the mine would be stranger than the harbor. She said she had no present experience there to answer that. He described the place through stories heard from travelers, then laughed at how quickly he had forgotten his own source limits. They shared an ordinary curiosity without treating it as a report ready for the association's seal.

shoal_e23_survey_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_18.text: At her room, she set the actual method packet beside her own practice notebook and did not merge their pages. One described unpowered external tools held for a dated loan. The other described six earned pairs and a renewed small local task. She could learn from ordinary measurement and still require qualified teaching for any new route. Carrying instruments did not create a seventh-stage examination in her pack.

shoal_e23_survey_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_19.text: On Day Four Hundred Twenty-One, the receiver confirmed the final selected preparation had finished within two offered hours. The survey source had spent twenty-four on carrier booking and four on performed permitted copying. Twenty-two remained for arrival board eight, two actual receiving days ten, and return dispatch four. No statement fund, port-owned plates, or household mandate appeared. Lin's personal provision remained separate from both tools and source.

shoal_e23_survey_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_survey_20.text: She closed her own pack with the accepted loan extract inside its ordinary cover. The carrier would handle the case on the actual departure date, and the mine would receive it under the offered current permissions when reached. Lin had chosen an independent way to ask limited questions and an obligation to return the means of asking them. The road would not become easier merely because she now had a level.

shoal_e23_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_01.text: The two selected preparation visits were complete. Their current receiving had changed the road from a title into actual people, property, bookings, and permissions. Mine wages remained future, arrival support remained future, and physical departure had not occurred. Lin went to Sui's ordinary desk with the role extract and her own application record. The captain preferred to check those current facts before everyone became hurried on the loading morning.

shoal_e23_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_02.text: Sui asked where the funded scope ended. Lin named the actual receiving days and current obligations, including any selected property return. The captain checked the chosen terms without claiming authority over the mine's later work. Ordinary travel receiving could help the next town understand what Lin arrived with. It could not hire her there or transform her body record into an exemption from the place's current entry process.

shoal_e23_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_03.text: The departure lane would be crowded on Four Hundred Twenty-Five. Sui named the actual passenger window and ordinary waiting area, then asked Lin to arrive before the last bell. Lin agreed and wrote it down. The captain said travelers who knew a port too well often became less punctual, assuming someone would bend a rule for a familiar face. Friendship could make leaving pleasant without making the carrier's clock less real.

shoal_e23_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_04.text: Lin stopped at the public room where Han was receiving requests under his ordinary continuing hours. A visitor had heard she would leave and brought a whole stack of doubtful sources. Her special review appointment had closed. Han offered the current process and accepted what belonged to his own scope. Lin did not remain to solve the stack because a departure rumor made the visitor feel his last chance had arrived.

shoal_e23_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_05.text: The visitor was unhappy. He had delayed asking and now wanted Lin's current time to replace the time he had lost. She could regret the pressure he felt and still keep her completed job closed. Han named the next qualified request window. The man took its actual date and left the stack in proper temporary custody. The office had an ordinary path for him after Lin's road began.

shoal_e23_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_06.text: He Ming had begun preparing the wider labor-receiving proposal with consenting workers who offered actual hours. Lin read the current public draft only when invited under its permitted scope. It contained disputed questions and no guaranteed adoption. She pointed out a line that joined carrier receiving and wages too loosely. The group considered her observation and decided its own wording. Her departure would not suspend their project or make them await her return.

shoal_e23_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_07.text: One worker wanted Lin's name on the proposal because she was known. She declined a role she would not perform after leaving and offered permission for the narrow current observation she had actually supplied. A familiar name could attract attention and create a false expectation of who would answer later questions. The workers chose actual continuing contacts instead. That gave the proposal less borrowed prestige and a clearer working future.

shoal_e23_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_08.text: At the school wall, the alarm diagram had received a small ordinary repair after weather loosened its cover. The teacher's own current maintenance scope paid the work. Children had added more openly imagined pictures beside it, including a paper boat shaped like a palace. Lin stopped to look. The corrected account and the imagined palace could share a wall because their purposes were visible, not because one had become evidence for the other.

shoal_e23_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_09.text: The child who drew the palace asked whether she would send a picture from the mine. Lin promised no image she could not yet make and offered an ordinary letter if a suitable permitted source and route later existed. He preferred a picture but accepted the narrow answer. His teacher said he could draw his own imagined mine meanwhile. The child began immediately, unconcerned that Lin's actual current map did not support its enormous towers.

shoal_e23_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_10.text: Bo had reduced his shop hours further after the apprentice's accepted departure to more paid work elsewhere. He kept the remaining tasks within current staff and his body limits. Jin still had her own net repair, which did not become unpaid shop labor by proximity. shoal_e23_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_11.text: Bo said a customer had finally accepted that a restored stool might show its old repair. shoal_e23_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_12.text: He asked whether she wanted to keep the little rule after its return. It belonged to him, and he was now offering it as an actual gift. Lin declined because he used it at the shop and she could buy her own if later work required one. Bo did not interpret the refusal as rejecting him. He put it back where the apprentice had made a proper place for it and offered a simpler farewell instead.

shoal_e23_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_13.text: Jin asked Lin to write only if she wanted, using their offered ordinary contact route. She did not ask for proof that the mine was better than the harbor. Some people simply needed another kind of work for the season they were in.

shoal_e23_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_14.text: The innkeeper asked for Lin's actual final departure time so he could arrange the next guest's room receiving. She had paid through the accepted last port date and assumed no refund for leaving earlier in that period. The keeper would clean and inspect under his own ordinary scope after she returned the key. He wanted no private practice pages left behind and no promise that she would take any future bed he offered.

shoal_e23_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_15.text: She sorted her paper that evening. Private body notes stayed in her pack. Permitted copies kept their current source limits. Institution originals and temporary custody records had already returned to their named holders. She tore up an obsolete blank booking draft that could confuse a later reader if mistaken for an accepted agreement. The real selected road copy remained whole. Leaving could be practical work long before the first wheel moved.

shoal_e23_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_16.text: Her old uneven cup was too awkward for the narrow road pack she wanted. She asked the innkeeper whether he wanted it for ordinary flowers and described its unstable foot. He accepted that actual gift, with no promise to keep it forever. The newer cup would travel with her. shoal_e23_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_17.text: At supper she spent no more than the personal extras already bounded for the stay. The regular meal belonged to her current two-copper room-and-meal rate. She listened to a courier describe a delayed boat and an ordinary family guest complain about pepper. The table would continue making such arguments after her departure. She liked knowing the inn could remain itself without preparing a special ending around the traveler who happened to be leaving.

shoal_e23_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_18.text: Before bed she counted own cash and confirmed the thirty road living provision separately from any institutional fare or arrival support. Her conservative remaining margin would stay at least forty-four after those planned road costs, with any actual positive branch receipts additional. shoal_e23_rejoin_19.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_19.text: On Day Four Hundred Twenty-One's final evening, the public lane carried summer smells of salt, bread, and damp rope. Lin took a short ordinary walk with no powered task. shoal_e23_rejoin_20.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_20.text: She returned to her room before the tower's night hour and checked the actual departure time once more. shoal_e23_rejoin_21.speaker: narrator
shoal_e23_rejoin_21.text: At the landing, the innkeeper had cleared the ordinary rear exit before closing his shop. Lin checked her own path once and left his work alone. A familiar building still deserved attention on the final nights spent inside it.
